1.why: All ten screens are static, single-column pages with no animation, video, pop-ups, or modals observed.

2.why: Key notices use coloured callout banners and primary actions are bold blue buttons, though the dark activity-log console and repeated security block visually compete with them.

3.why: Each screen presents one labelled input and one primary button near the top, so Helena can find the needed control without searching or scrolling.

4.why: The user must track a six-stage flow and satisfy four password rules including the technical '72 UTF-8 bytes (bcrypt limit)' rule, plus keep in mind that tokens expire quickly and work once.

5.why: No 'remember me', autofill, password-manager support, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: The token prefilled in step 3 matches the token shown in step 2 so it can be recognised, but no saved personal items such as Helena's email address are ever displayed.

7.why: Most labels and banners are short plain-language sentences, although jargon like 'UTF-8 bytes (bcrypt limit)' and the 64-character hex token hurt readability.

8.why: Only informational and success banners appear in the screenshots; no error message describing a problem and its fix is shown at any step.

9.why: Helper text explains manual token submission and the demo banners display the exact code to type, but no illustrative examples such as a sample email or password format are given.

10.why: The system forces a single fixed sequence of email, token, code, and password and never offers alternative login choices such as face login, so no clear choice between methods exists.

11.why: Every screen offers at most one primary action plus an occasional 'Start over' button, so the user is never faced with many choices at once.

12.why: Each action is followed by an explicit outcome banner and timestamped log entry, e.g. 'Recovery token verified' and the final 'Recovery complete' confirmation.

13.why: Short tips accompany new steps, such as 'A token from the recovery link can be submitted manually here' and the password-requirement bullets, though some tips are technical.

14.why: Only the 'Start over' button on the delivery screen offers a restart; no retry or back option is visible on the token, code, or password steps, and one-time expiring tokens penalise mistakes.

15.why: All ten steps reuse the same header, card layout, banner styles, buttons, and 'Keep your account safe' block, making the design highly consistent and learnable.
